title: One-hour high-sensitivity troponin rule-out for a district hospital chest pain unit: a rapid review of safety, yield and sampling failures
abstract: Objective: to summarise the 30-day safety of one-hour troponin rule-out, the proportion of patients ruled out overall and in older and kidney patients, time saved, and second-sample timing failures. Design: rapid review updating a 2022 meta-analysis with a dated search from June 2021 and stated shortcuts. Results and conclusions will be written after the synthesis.
introduction: One-hour rule-out pathways promise shorter stays, but most evidence comes from specialist centres with younger patients. A district hospital where 38 percent of attendances are aged 75 or over needs to know the likely yield and failure points before adopting one.
methods: Three databases were searched from June 2021 and the 2022 meta-analysis's studies were included. One reviewer screened with a 20 percent check; safety and yield values were double-checked. Proportions were pooled on the logit scale with random effects; conference abstracts were listed but not graded or pooled.
results: No studies have been screened yet. The report will present the search flow, pooled 30-day safety, yield overall and by age and kidney function, time in the department and timing failures.
discussion: The discussion will set the likely local yield against the safety estimate, describe the sampling and laboratory conditions under which the pathway worked, and state what the unit should monitor after any change.
limitations: Rapid review shortcuts; English only; subgroup data sparse; one ungraded conference abstract.
conclusion: To be written after the synthesis; it will not extrapolate safety to groups the studies did not include.
reportingChecklist: PRISMA 2020, with the rapid review shortcuts listed
summary: PRISMA-structured draft with results left empty until the synthesis.
